Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

sheepdog (development version)

  • compare_calibration_curves() takes several targets in one call (target = c(0.90, 0.95)): the curves and the cross-validation are fitted once per group, and the result gains a target column, with one row per group x target x curve. The new argument cv = FALSE skips the cross-validation when only the thresholds and the verdict are needed.

  • select_clips(sampling_mode = "score_bands") accepts strata = "species", which pools the sites and draws n_top clips per species x score band, for a threshold of the species when the cut per site x band would be too coarse.

  • threshold_bootstrap(), suggest_thresholds() and the other functions built on the empirical threshold are faster: the precision at every candidate cut is computed in one pass over the clips sorted by score, with the same result (about ten times faster in a bootstrap of 360 clips).

  • Bug fix: select_clips(sampling_mode = "random_recordings", sites = ) now restricts the list of recordings to sites; it only filtered the predictions, so every site of recordings was drawn.

  • New warning_signs(): for each species, the warning signs of the threshold workflow that a review sample can show (1, low recall ceiling, from recall_ceiling(); 2, the threshold discards most true positives; 6, false-positive rates that vary by site or season, with the main confusing identity; 7, a threshold below target in some group, from threshold_by_group(); 8, a logistic curve wrong near the threshold, from compare_calibration_curves()), and a verdict: "trustworthy_with_care", "use_with_caveats" or "not_trustworthy". Optionally writes the report as Markdown.

  • New recall_ceiling(): from the occasions of "random_recordings" annotated by ear and the highest score of the species in each, the recall ceiling (share of the occasions with the species that have any prediction at or above min_confidence) and the recall at one or more thresholds (a vector, or a table of thresholds per group such as the output of suggest_thresholds() or threshold_bootstrap()), weighted by 1 / inclusion_prob, with intervals from a bootstrap of whole recordings. Also reports the occasions with the species and no prediction (n_missed). The validation-effort vignette gains a section on it.

  • New compare_calibration_curves(): checks the shape of the calibration curve before a threshold is taken from it. For each species (or by group), fits the logistic in the logit of the score, a quadratic, a GAM (mgcv) and a monotone GAM (scam), weighted by 1 / inclusion_prob when the clips have it, and reports the cross-validated log-loss (folds of whole recordings), the calibration error in the high score bins, the thresholds of each curve (probability and precision rules) against the weighted count of suggest_thresholds(), and a verdict from the decision table of the threshold workflow ("keep_logistic", "use_monotone_or_weighted", "no_curve_reaches_target", "sample_more_near_threshold"). plot_calibration_curves() draws the curves over the observed precision by bin. mgcv and scam join Suggests; a curve whose package is missing is left out with a message. The calibration vignette gains a section on it.

  • The Setup tab of run_app() offers sampling_mode = "score_bands", with its strata and score bands; fields the mode does not take (total and maximum per species, threshold) are not passed on. The vignette sampling-designs gains a section on the mode.

  • New sampling_mode = "score_bands" in select_clips(): n_top clips drawn at random in each stratum x score band (score_breaks, default 0.1, 0.4, 0.7, 1), with inclusion_prob = drawn / candidates of the stratum x band. These clips are meant for thresholds and calibration curves across the whole score range, not for the false-positive rate of an occupancy model, because they were chosen by their score. The documentation of select_clips() gains a table of which design serves which use. export_occupancy_data() warns that crywolf drops these clips.

  • New threshold_bootstrap(): the uncertainty of the threshold of suggest_thresholds() by resampling whole recordings (or nights) within each cell, with a conservative threshold (an upper quantile) and the share of replicates that reach the target.

  • New threshold_by_group(): the precision that one threshold per cell gives in each month, hour or other group, flagging the groups below the target.

  • New threshold_record(): one table (and optionally a Markdown file) with the threshold, its interval, the groups below the target and the provenance of the clips.

  • run_app(blind = TRUE): blind review, which hides the score, the sampling design and the clip file name, and shuffles the queue once per reviewer.

  • New select_directed(): a review round aimed by a model. Units (such as site x month x species) are drawn with probability proportional to a size, typically the expected gain of a review, with a floor that keeps every unit drawable; one candidate occasion is drawn in each unit and all its predictions >= threshold become clips. The manifest has sampling_mode = "directed_pps" and inclusion_prob = probability of the unit / candidate occasions of the unit; the units and their inclusion probabilities are returned in the attribute "units". Clips of earlier rounds (previous) are left out.

  • export_occupancy_data() writes clips of "directed_pps" to validation.csv, with review_scope = "occasion" when every prediction of the occasion has a verdict, as in "random_detections". The warning about clips in more than one design now covers every pair of designs.

  • The Review tab of run_app() has an optional Identity field for what a negative or uncertain clip is (free text or suggestions from the manifest classes and the new identity_categories()), marked sure or probable. The verdicts file gains the columns identity and identity_certainty; files of earlier versions are still read, and are rewritten once with the new columns at their next verdict. app_verdicts() returns both columns.

  • New join_identities(): adds identities recorded outside the app (a spreadsheet with one row per clip) to a table of verdicts, keeping those of the app and warning about identities on clips that are not negative.

  • New confuser_summary(): for each target class, the identities of its negative clips, flagging those that are classes of the classifier.

  • run_app(), review_queue() and post_validation() stop with a clear error when the manifest file is empty (0 bytes or only the header) or missing, instead of reporting missing columns. An empty (0-byte) verdicts_file also stops with a clear error, since new verdicts would be written without the header.

  • export_occupancy_data() writes schema 1.4, which only adds to 1.3: n_windows in occasions.csv (new argument window_step), round, stratum, n_candidates, n_drawn and review_scope in validation.csv, and the design of the draw in schema.json (new argument candidates). The version no longer depends on the tables written.

  • The stage figures now also appear in the vignettes and articles, with new figures on where false positives come from and on occupancy with false positives. The site has a new Cheat sheets tab, with a cheat sheet and an illustrated guide by Larissa S. M. Sugai to download.

  • New threshold_history(): the nightly history of the empirical route, from the thresholds of review_support(), with no calibration model. Nights of cells without a threshold stay in the history as effort, with NA in the detection columns.

  • previous in select_clips() and extract_validation_clips() also takes the reviews of the other random design ("random_detections" and "random_recordings"). The draw stays independent, and previously_reviewed marks the clips that overlap an earlier review. With the new inherit = TRUE, clips whose verdict follows from that review get inherited_verdict: an absent recording makes its predictions negative, a positive prediction makes its recording present. cut_clips() and the review app skip them, post_validation() fills them in, and export_occupancy_data() leaves them out with a warning, as they repeat a judgement and are chosen by their verdict. It also warns about occasions in both validation and recordings_verified, which a model takes as two independent reviews (#102).

  • New compare_thresholds(): the thresholds of suggest_thresholds() and calibrated_thresholds() side by side for each site x species, with a flag that compares the empirical and the model-precision thresholds, the calibration_quality() status and a mark for model thresholds above the highest reviewed score. post_validation(fit = ) writes it to thresholds_compared.csv (#104).

  • suggest_thresholds() gains sustained: with TRUE, the target precision must also hold at every higher cut with at least min_n clips, the rule of calibrated_thresholds(). The default, FALSE, keeps the thresholds as they were, because the empirical precision of high cuts is noisy; the documentation gives the cost (#104).

  • Review rounds: select_clips() and extract_validation_clips() gain previous, candidates and cells, to draw another round of a design without repeating what was reviewed. In "random_detections", the occasions drawn earlier leave the pool and the rounds together are a simple random sample of each stratum. The first round writes candidates.csv, later rounds draw from it, and a different threshold, occasion_unit or strata, or a cap, is refused. Manifests gain round, n_candidates, n_drawn and inclusion_prob_round. The new combine_rounds(), also through read_validation_tables(candidates = ) and post_validation(previous = ), gives every clip the cumulative inclusion_prob; review_support() then adds n_rounds and reached_last_round. vignette("validation-effort") measures the bias of stopping when a cell reaches the target (#107).

  • suggest_thresholds(): weighted cells no longer fail when the highest score rounds up past itself (0.996 gives the cut 1).

  • suggest_thresholds() now chooses the cut with the precision weighted by 1 / inclusion_prob in the cells whose clips all have it, as "random_detections" draws strata with unequal probabilities. min_n applies there to Kish’s effective sample size, given in n_eff, and precision_used says which precision chose each cut. Thresholds of such cells can change; weighted = FALSE, also in post_validation() and review_support(), restores the previous choice. Cells that mix clips with and without inclusion_prob use the unweighted precision, with a warning. Tables without inclusion_prob are unchanged (#103).

  • New calibration_quality(): checks the calibrated probabilities by species (or by cell) on held-out clips, with the gain in log-loss over a null model, the AUC of the probabilities and of the raw score within the group, the calibration intercept and slope, and a status. The measures of compare_calibration_models() cover all the clips and can hide a species whose score says little. calibrate() writes calibration_quality.csv, returns quality and names the groups marked "poor".

  • select_clips(): "random_detections" now says so when every candidate occasion was taken (all inclusion_prob equal to 1), which is a census and not a random draw.

  • run_app(): the app opens on a new Intro tab with a graphical abstract of the sampling designs and an Audio panel, where the audio folder (new audio_dir argument, listed into recordings.csv), the BirdNET results and the validation folder can be chosen with the system’s folder dialog. Folders given to run_app() are confirmed when the app opens, and run_app() can be called without arguments. The panel shows the recordings per site and night, coloured by the share of hours with predictions of the chosen species, with the number of predictions on hover.

  • run_app(): every field has a short help note; the threshold is marked “(required)” for "random_detections". After each draw the Sampling tab checks that the recordings exist and, with Audio folder, finds moved recordings by file name and offers to use them. A cut that finds no audio says so, and a manifest without cut clips no longer stops the app from opening.

  • run_app(), Review tab: the spectrogram has a palette, the FFT window, the maximum frequency (12 kHz by default, also max_freq), brightness and contrast above it, uses 90% overlap, and a dashed line follows the audio. The clip number is shown above the spectrogram, and space now plays or pauses the clip (the right arrow moves to the next one).

  • New argument site_pattern of list_recordings(), read_selection_tables(), extract_validation_clips() and run_app() (also a field of the Audio panel): a regular expression with one capture group that takes the site from the file name, for recordings or tables of several sites in one folder.

  • run_app(): the moved-recording check of the Sampling tab reuses the list of the audio folder made by the Audio panel instead of scanning the folder again at each draw, and the folder dialog also works on Linux (through ‘tcltk’, when there is a display).

  • The review-app article describes the Intro tab, the Audio panel and its recording summary, site_pattern and the spectrogram controls, and gives the new default of max_freq (12 kHz).

  • post_validation() reads the verdicts of the review app: with verdicts_file (and optionally reviewer) it takes the verdicts from run_app() instead of the review folders, combines clips reviewed by more than one reviewer with consensus_verdicts() and writes the same outputs. review_dir is then optional and only fills reviewed_path.

  • precision_by_bin() adds precision_weighted and suggest_thresholds() adds precision_weighted_at_threshold when the reviewed clips carry inclusion_prob ("random_detections"): the precision weighted by 1 / inclusion_prob, which estimates the precision among all the predictions rather than among the reviewed clips. The thresholds are still chosen from the unweighted precision, and tables without inclusion_prob are unchanged.

  • app_verdicts() reports how many clips a reviewer marked more than once and how many of them changed verdict (the last verdict counts).

  • New list_recordings(): builds the list of all recordings (site, source_audio) from the audio folders, including those without any prediction, for recordings in select_clips(), export_occupancy_data() and run_app(). The site is the first folder below the root; remap_from/remap_to rewrite the prefix to match Begin Path, and predictions checks that the audio files of the predictions are in the list. It can write recordings.csv (#81).

  • New article, “Organising the data”: the folder layout sheepdog expects, file names, the paths written by BirdNET and the list of recordings.

  • New calibrated_thresholds(): confidence thresholds per site and species from the calibration model of stage 2 (fit_calibration()), following Wood & Kahl (2024), instead of from the reviewed clips of each cell alone as in suggest_thresholds(). rule = "probability" gives the lowest score at which P(TP) reaches the target; rule = "precision" the lowest score at which the expected precision of the detections kept, from score_detections(), reaches it. With a brms model, a conservative threshold from the lower quantile of the posterior is added. The calibration vignette has a new section. The default target, 0.95, is the p_min of score_detections() and calibrate().

  • calibrate() writes thresholds.csv and returns thresholds: the calibrated_thresholds() of each site x species with rule = "probability" and target = p_min, the score equivalent of the cut on P(TP) used for the detection histories.

  • The sampling-designs vignette opens with a figure that matches each design to the question it answers, and the calibration vignette has a guide to choosing a confidence threshold.

  • read_selection_tables() also reads the per-audio selection tables that the BirdNET GUI writes by default (<audio>.BirdNET.selection.table.txt, new argument per_audio_pattern), besides the combined table of each site (BirdNET_SelectionTable.txt, written when “Combine selection tables” is checked). The per-audio tables of a folder are stacked and the Selection column is renumbered, which gives the same result as the combined table. score_detections(), calibrate() and extract_validation_clips() accept them too: in tables and prediction_tables, give the folder of a site instead of the path of its combined table. The vignettes say where each format comes from.

  • export_occupancy_data(species = ) now filters by the species asked for. The argument was masked by the species column of the predictions, so any value left no prediction and stopped the export. select_clips() uses the same filter and is protected the same way.

  • export_occupancy_data() gains min_verified (default 10) and warns about species with predictions but fewer reviewed detection clips, or without any positive or any negative clip: their false-positive rates will rest on the other species or on the prior. A simulation in dev/verification-by-species/ shows that no sampling design of select_clips() gives a truly rare species enough reviewed clips.

  • New fixture of the data contract, tests/testthat/fixtures/export-1.3-ms (built by data-raw/make_export_fixture_ms.R), shared with crywolf for its multi-species model: three species of the example data, one of them rare (detected at two sites, 15 reviewed clips per site), with a calibration on temperature and species and site x species effects. The contract tests check that every table and the occasion versions keep their keys by species, and that crywolf reads each species with the versions of the export.

  • dev/roadmap-integration.md: CRAN submissions of sheepdog 3.3.2 and crywolf 2.1.0, and steps 5 to 7 of crywolf::fp_occu_dyn().

  • dev/roadmap-integration.md: step 8 of crywolf::fp_occu_dyn() (blocked cross-validation on the Curiango data) and the multi-species model (phase 5) moved ahead of phase 2, with the sheepdog side of it: a multi-species fixture of the data contract and a check of verification per species.

sheepdog 3.3.3

Resubmission to CRAN, answering the review of 3.3.2. The installed code is the same as 3.3.2.

  • DESCRIPTION cites the methods the package implements: the multiple-method (Miller et al. 2011) and observation-confirmation (Chambert et al. 2015) designs and the conversion of confidence scores into probabilities (Wood & Kahl 2024).
  • Additional_repositories lists only https://diogoprov.r-universe.dev (for crywolf, in Suggests); the repository of cmdstanr, which sheepdog does not use, is no longer declared.

sheepdog 3.3.2

Submission candidate for CRAN, replacing 3.3.1 (never uploaded).

  • occasion_draws() reads calibration_draws.parquet without memory mapping, so the file is no longer locked on Windows after the call (it could not be removed or replaced, and a test failed on win-builder).

sheepdog 3.3.1

Submission candidate for CRAN, replacing 3.3.0 (never uploaded). The installed package is the same as 3.3.0, apart from the vignette below.

  • vignette("crywolf-integration") cites the Curiango article as accepted, without its DOI, which the publisher has not yet registered (the link failed the URL check).

Repository only

  • Test coverage is uploaded to Codecov, with a badge in the README; the coverage checks are informational and never block a merge.
  • dev/benchmarks/curiango-export.R: CALIB_COVARIATE adds a night covariate to the calibration (schema 1.3) and ADAPT_DELTA is passed to brms; curiango-flow.R reads such exports and takes CLASSIFIERS. On the Curiango, a calibration with night temperature restores the temperature effect on occupancy that the Monte Carlo path had lost with the custom classifier.
  • dev/benchmarks/: curiango-mc-stability.R (choice of the number of versions M of the Monte Carlo propagation) and curiango-fig4-mc.R (the Monte Carlo path beside the threshold paths of the Curiango article); curiango-flow.R can save the draws of each fit (DRAWS_DIR).
  • inst/benchmarks/curiango-mc-stability.csv: stability of the pooled Monte Carlo summaries of the Curiango by number of versions (M = 2-50). Rule of thumb, from a pilot run: M = 100 x the largest between-fit share of the variance keeps the Monte Carlo error under 10% of the posterior SD.

sheepdog 3.3.0

This release adds the data contract with the crywolf package and the Monte Carlo propagation of the calibration (phases 0 and 1 of the integration), a local app to draw, review and export clips, and the splits and checks for retraining BirdNET-Analyzer.

  • Integration with crywolf: export_occupancy_data() (schema sheepdog-occupancy 1.1-1.3), occasion_draws(), calibration_ppc(), covariate_bins() and a contract test against crywolf.
  • Review: run_app(), app_verdicts() and review_support().
  • Retraining: build_training_set() with splits by night, a validation set by night, a cap per site x species and non-event negatives; training_nights() and exclude_training_clips() by recording or night.

All changes

  • build_training_set() gains negatives_folder: with a non-event class of BirdNET-Analyzer (e.g. "Noise"), every negative goes to that folder, named <species>-<site>-<clip_file>, instead of a -<species_code> folder. In BirdNET-Analyzer 2.4.0 those folders get the label -1, which makes the loss unbounded and inflates the validation AUPRC (BirdNET-Analyzer issue 1033); the documentation recommends "Noise" until this is fixed. NULL, the default, keeps the previous layout.
  • build_training_set() gains val_prop and val_seed: a validation set by night, drawn from the training nights left after the test draw and the cap, never from exclude_from_test, written to val/ to be passed as --test_data. It gives the same split as a second call on the training rows (checked on the FrogNet M3 training set: 288 nights and 824 clips). The checks gain val_nights_in_train and val_nights_excluded.
  • run_app() gains the Sampling and Export tabs, opened with selection_dir and output_dir. Sampling is a form for the design of select_clips(): Draw shows the clips per site and species and their inclusion probabilities, and warns that "top" clips do not estimate the false-positive rate; Cut clips calls cut_clips() (or simulates it) and writes clip_manifest.csv, extraction_info.csv and clips/, and the new clips go straight to the Review tab. Export calls export_occupancy_data() with the verdicts of the app (combined by consensus_verdicts() across reviewers) and shows the summary of schema.json. New arguments recordings and classifier; run_app(manifest, clips_dir) works as before.
  • New run_app(): a local ‘shiny’ app to review the clips one at a time, with spectrogram, player, the data of each clip and keyboard shortcuts (p, n, u, arrows); max_freq limits the spectrogram band. Each verdict ("positive", "negative" or "uncertain") is appended at once to a CSV file, so an interrupted review resumes where it stopped; with a manifest from assign_reviewers(), each reviewer sees only their clips. New app_verdicts() turns that file into the table of classify_review(), so the rest of stage 1, the agreement between reviewers and the calibration work unchanged. New article “Sampling, reviewing and exporting in the sheepdog app”. ‘shiny’ joins Suggests.
  • exclude_training_clips() with a table of training_nights() and level = "recording" reads source_audio with the pattern given to training_nights() (kept in the attribute "pattern" of its table), or with the new argument pattern, instead of always the default pattern; it warns when no source_audio matches, instead of excluding nothing in silence.
  • build_training_set() gains split: "site" (the previous behaviour, with test_sites), "night" (a proportion test_prop of the nights of each site goes to the test set, for all species together), "site_species_night" (nights drawn within site x species, as in the 2.x FrogNet scripts; warns, since a night can then be in both sets) and "none". The draws use seed and leave the global random number generator as it was. New arguments: max_per_site_species (cap on the positive training clips of a site x species, taken from the nights in turn), exclude_from_test (nights that must stay out of the test set), copy = FALSE (write only training_set.csv), remap_from / remap_to and strict. The result gains night and the attribute "checks": test nights with training clips, test nights in exclude_from_test and test clips overlapping training clips. On the FrogNet M3 data, the result is identical clip by clip to the reference script for split = "night" and "site_species_night".
  • New training_nights(): site, recording and night from the names of training clips (a configurable regular expression, folders listed recursively, site_map, night_cutoff), for exclude_from_test and exclude_training_clips().
  • exclude_training_clips() gains level ("clip", the previous behaviour, "recording" or "night") and any_species, and takes the table of training_nights().
  • The README figures are redrawn (data-raw/diagram_pipeline.R, data-raw/diagram_extraction.R): the pipeline shows the reviewers, the model selection by log-loss, the Bayesian calibration and its checks, review_support(), cell_status(), community_matrices_draws() and the occupancy branch (export_occupancy_data() > occasion_draws() > crywolf); the extraction flow shows the strata of "random_detections" and covariate_bins(). The README function table lists covariate_bins(), review_support(), calibration_ppc(), export_occupancy_data() and occasion_draws().
  • The contract test reads the fixture export-1.3 in crywolf as well (with crywolf >= 2.1.0.9000): fp_draws_data() returns the versions of occasion_draws.parquet and refuses a different seed.
  • New review_support(): for each site x species cell, the reviewed clips at high scores, their precision, the high-score detections not yet reviewed, the threshold of suggest_thresholds() and a diagnosis ("reached", "exhausted", "unreliable", "review more", "not reviewed"). It replaces the code of the support table of vignette("validation-effort") and gives the same result. With by and covariates (e.g. from covariate_bins()), the diagnosis is repeated within the bins of an environmental gradient or acoustic index, counting the unreviewed detections by bin too.
  • export_occupancy_data() exports a calibration on continuous covariates of the occasion (tp ~ logit_conf + temp_z), schema sheepdog-occupancy 1.3: P(TP) is computed for each prediction, the versions of the detections are drawn in the export and written to occasion_draws.parquet, and calibration_draws.parquet is not written. schema.json records the covariates (calibration$covariates), their range in the calibration data and their standardisation (covariate_scaling). New arguments n_versions, rule, p_min and covariate_scaling; without covariates, n_versions calls occasion_draws() on the folder (schema 1.2). occasion_draws() refuses a folder of schema 1.3, which has no grid. New fixture tests/testthat/fixtures/export-1.3, checked by the contract test. Agreed with crywolf (dev/proposal-calibration-covariates.md there), which will read version 1.3 later.
  • calibration_prior() gives other population-level terms, such as a continuous covariate, a normal(0, 1) prior; the slope of logit_conf then keeps normal(1, 1) without the truncation at 0, since ‘brms’ cannot bound a single coefficient.
  • New covariate_bins() cuts a covariate of the occasions (an environmental gradient, such as the temperature of the night, or an acoustic index of the recording or minute) into bins, by default quantiles within each site. select_clips() gains covariates, so that the "random_detections" draw can be stratified by those bins (strata = "temp_bin") with exact inclusion probabilities, and a message recalls that a stratum related to the verdict should enter the calibration. precision_by_bin(), suggest_thresholds() and cell_status() gain by, to check each site x species cell within the bins. vignette("validation-effort") has a new section, “Stage 1 along a gradient”, with both examples and their caveats.
  • man/sheepdog-package.Rd lists the three authors (it was not regenerated when Authors@R changed).
  • vignette("crywolf-integration"): the Curiango data come from seven recorders, not four, and the calibration model is chosen among three candidates, not two.
  • Larissa S. M. Sugai and Liliana Piatti, who designed the validation protocol, are now listed as authors (Authors@R and CITATION.cff).
  • New export_occupancy_data() writes, in one folder, the data of an occupancy model with false positives (schema sheepdog-occupancy, version 1): every occasion, with or without predictions (occasions.csv), the predictions above min_confidence (detections.csv) and their highest score per occasion x species (scores.csv), the reviewed clips with their design and inclusion probability (validation.csv), the recordings annotated by ear (recordings_verified.csv), the site covariates (sites.csv) and, with a model fitted with engine = "brms", posterior draws of P(TP) on a grid of scores (calibration_draws.parquet). schema.json records the version of the schema and the settings of the export. vignette("crywolf-integration") documents every column.
  • ‘jsonlite’ is imported and ‘arrow’ is suggested, for the export.
  • export_occupancy_data() drops predictions that repeat the site, recording, offset and species of another (e.g. a selection table read twice), with a warning, and warns when most occasion x species with several predictions share a single score, a sign that one score per occasion was copied to several rows.
  • export_occupancy_data() writes version 1.1 of the sheepdog-occupancy schema, which only adds to version 1: occasion_covariates appends covariates of the occasions (matched by occasion_id or by recording) to occasions.csv, and calibration_keys exports a calibration that depends on a property of the occasion, such as the month (tp ~ logit_conf + (1 | month)): each key becomes a text column of occasions.csv and of calibration_draws.parquet, which covers every level found among the occasions (levels absent from the calibration data are drawn as new levels). schema.json lists them in occasion_covariates and calibration$keys. A small export of the example data in this schema, made by data-raw/make_export_fixture.R, is shared with crywolf as a test fixture.
  • New occasion_draws() turns an export with calibration draws into one version of the detection data per posterior draw: in each draw an occasion is a detection when at least one of its predictions is judged true, either at random with its probability of being true ("sample") or above p_min ("threshold"). It writes occasion_draws.parquet in the export (schema version 1.2), so that any occupancy software can propagate the uncertainty of the calibration. The random numbers follow those of crywolf::fp_draws_data(), and a test checks that both give the same detections; tests/testthat/fixtures/export-1.2/ holds the shared case.
  • vignette("crywolf-integration") runs the whole flow on the Curiango data (one-minute recordings, two classifiers): export, posterior predictive check of the calibration, occasion_draws() and the Monte Carlo propagation in crywolf (fp_draws_data(), fp_occu_mc()), with results cached in inst/benchmarks/curiango-flow-*.csv.
  • A contract test (tests/testthat/test-contract.R, the counterpart of crywolf’s test-read_sheepdog.R) checks that exports follow the schema documented in vignette("crywolf-integration"): the fields of schema.json and the row counts it declares, the columns and keys of every table, scores.csv against detections.csv, calibration keys as text covering every level of the occasions, and the layout of occasion_draws.parquet. With crywolf installed, it also checks that crywolf reads each export and the stored occasion draws.
  • New calibration_ppc() checks a Bayesian calibration model against the reviewed clips: the observed share of true positives against its posterior predictive distribution, overall and by score bin, site, species and any column of the validation data (e.g. month), with a mid-p Bayesian p-value. plot_calibration_ppc() draws one check.
  • vignette("sampling-designs") gains a section on recorders that run the classifier on the device and discard the audio: keep a probability sample of the raw audio, drawn without looking at the scores, so that the calibration and the false-positive rate can still be estimated.
  • The v1.2.0 reproduction test compares the auc_sd column of the effort curve with a relative tolerance of 1e-2 (1e-3 elsewhere): with lme4 2.1-0 this standard deviation over three small fits moves by about 0.4%.

sheepdog 3.2.1

  • Added fast tests for posterior matrix uncertainty, training provenance, overlap boundaries, missing clips and degenerate reviewer agreement.
  • Corrected the minimum dplyr version for join relationship checks.
  • Fixed the performance article index and replaced an unresolved manuscript DOI link with the validated Zenodo data citation.
  • Declared the repositories needed by the optional crywolf integration in Additional_repositories for CRAN checks.

sheepdog 3.2.0

  • calibration_models(single_species = TRUE) provides global and site- effect candidates for one species, including an optional uncorrelated site-slope model. calibrate() and compare_calibration_models() automatically choose candidates from the observed species and sites; explicit model lists still override automatic selection in the latter. The multispecies candidate family and its ordering are unchanged.
  • New performance vignette summarises the Curiango benchmark, regression checks and a reproducible multispecies simulation with held-out nights.

sheepdog 3.1.0

  • cell_status() includes both observed score endpoints in its grid and never extrapolates below the reviewed minimum. Crossings between 0.99 and the reviewed maximum are no longer missed.
  • New calibration_folds() exposes reproducible fold assignments. compare_calibration_models() and calibrate() accept fold_group, e.g. "source_audio" or "night", to keep groups intact across species within a site. The default clip assignment is unchanged.
  • read_validations(keep = ) optionally retains grouping metadata; calibrate() requests it automatically and saves grouped assignments in calibration_folds.csv. Missing IDs and insufficient groups raise clear errors. Single-verdict test folds retain probability scores and have missing AUC without counting as failed fits.

sheepdog 3.0.0

Breaking changes

  • calibrate() and select_calibration_model() now default to "one_se_logloss": choose the simplest candidate within one standard error of the lowest cross-validated log-loss, excluding candidates singular in most folds unless all are singular (with a warning). Supply select = "best_auc" (or rule = "best_auc" in the selector) to retain the 2.x selection. The comparison table still reports all metrics and is ordered by AUC; its first row is not necessarily the selected model. See the migration guide for a reproducible example.

Documentation and infrastructure

  • Added the 2.x to 3.0.0 migration guide.
  • CI measures test coverage with covr and uploads an HTML report and Cobertura XML as workflow artifacts, without a third-party token.

Documentation

  • New article “Reviewing clips in the BirdNET GUI” (site only): the review in the Review tab of the BirdNET-Analyzer GUI, from the folder of clips to the Positive and Negative folders read by classify_review(), with screenshots in English and Portuguese (where the result folders are positivo and negativo), the regression panel of the GUI compared with the calibration of stage 2, and the review with several reviewers.

Sampling

  • select_clips(strata = ) gains the presets "hour" (pooling the nights), "week" (ISO week of the night) and "month", and accepts a character vector of column names for strata defined by the user, e.g. c("month", "moon") with a column added to the detections before the call. site and species_code are always added to the strata, columns that depend on the score (confidence, rank) are refused, and every stratum column must be constant within an occasion.

Calibration

  • fit_calibration() (and calibrate()) passes on the messages of lme4::glmer(), prefixed by lme4:, instead of hiding them; the message on singular fits is not repeated, since it already becomes a warning. Every message of the fit is kept in the attribute sheepdog_messages of the model, and calibrate() appends them to calibration_model.txt. The fits of the cross-validation folds and of the effort curve stay quiet.

sheepdog 2.2.0

Calibration

  • compare_calibration_models() also scores the predicted probabilities on the held-out folds: log-loss and Brier score (proper scoring rules), calibration intercept and slope, the share of singular fold fits (prop_singular) and the position of each model (complexity).
  • New select_calibration_model(), with the rules "best_auc" (the rule of 2.x) and "one_se_logloss" (the simplest model within one standard error of the lowest log-loss, leaving out singular fits). calibrate() takes the rule in select; the default stays "best_auc" until 3.0.0, when it becomes "one_se_logloss".
  • calibration_models(uncorrelated = TRUE) adds m5_species_x_site_uncorrelated, the m4 structure without the correlation between the species intercepts and slopes, which avoids the singular fits of m4; calibrate() takes it with uncorrelated = TRUE.

Bayesian calibration

  • fit_calibration() gains engine = "brms": the model is fitted with ‘brms’ (Bernoulli, logit link). The prior must be given explicitly. Convergence diagnostics run after the fit and warn when R-hat, the effective sample sizes or the divergent transitions fail the usual limits.
  • New calibration_prior(): a weakly informative example prior centred on an already calibrated score (slope 1, intercept at the mean logit score), with the slope truncated at 0, exponential(1) on the standard deviations and lkj(2) on the correlations; only the classes present in the formula are returned.
  • New prior_predictive_calibration() and plot_calibration_draws() for prior predictive checks and for the uncertainty of the fitted curve; calibration_diagnostics(); calibration_sensitivity(), a power-scaling sensitivity analysis with ‘priorsense’.
  • score_detections() with a ‘brms’ model computes the posterior on a grid of scores per site x species and returns p_tp (posterior mean), p_tp_lower and pr_reliable (posterior probability that P(TP) >= p_min).
  • detection_history() gains rule = c("mean", "probability") and prob_min: a detection is reliable when its posterior mean reaches p_min, or when pr_reliable reaches prob_min.
  • New history_draws() and community_matrices_draws(): the detection histories and the community matrices over posterior draws, with the posterior mean and an interval for each cell.
  • calibrate() gains engine, prior (a prior or a function of the selected formula, such as calibration_prior), brms_args, rule and prob_min; with ‘brms’ it also writes calibration_diagnostics.csv.
  • New vignette("bayesian-calibration"), precomputed.
  • ‘brms’, ‘posterior’ and ‘priorsense’ are suggested packages.

Sampling

  • select_clips() gains strata ("night_hour", the rule of 2.0.0, "night" or "site_species") for the occasion draw of "random_detections". With one recording per hour, the default stratum holds a single occasion and draws nothing; a coarser stratum makes the draw random. A coarser stratum combined with balance_by_hour = TRUE under a target or limit warns that inclusion_prob is conditional on the first draw.
  • extract_validation_clips() writes extraction_info.csv with the provenance of the run (date, versions of sheepdog and R, folder of the tables, the new classifier label and every argument of select_clips()).
  • The message on predictions dropped by min_confidence is no longer printed when none is dropped.

Review and retraining

  • New read_validation_tables(): stacks the validation_by_clip.csv tables of several sites or rounds with every column and verdict (unlike read_validations(), which keeps only what the calibration needs).
  • New build_training_set(): copies the reviewed clips into the training layout of BirdNET-Analyzer (positives in <species_code>/, negatives in -<species_code>/), with the sites in test_sites in a separate test folder for --test_data; writes training_set.csv and warns about classes with fewer positive files than min_files.
  • New exclude_training_clips(): drops from a manifest the clips that overlap a clip used in training (same species and recording).
  • vignette("retraining") uses the new functions.

Community matrices

  • New cell_status(): classifies each site x species cell of the calibration as "reliable" (the calibrated curve reaches p_min within the reviewed scores, with at least min_n clips), "probably_absent" (no true positive among the reviewed clips) or "unreliable", separating the absence of a species from a calibration that fails.
  • New suggest_core_species(): the species with no unreliable cell.
  • community_matrices() gains drop_empty (drop the site x month rows without any core species) and returns trials, the matrix of nights recorded with the dimensions of the species counts, for the Ntrials of a binomial model such as gllvm::gllvm().
  • vignette("community-matrices") uses the new functions.

Several reviewers

  • New assign_reviewers(): splits the clips of a manifest among reviewers, balanced within species, with a fraction (overlap) given to a second reviewer.
  • New split_by_reviewer(): copies each reviewer’s clips to their own folder tree for the BirdNET GUI.
  • New reviewer_agreement(): agreement and kappa per species on the clips reviewed more than once (Cohen’s kappa for two reviewers, Fleiss’ kappa otherwise).
  • New consensus_verdicts(): one verdict per clip; conflicting clips get verdict = "disagreement" and are left out of precision and calibration.

sheepdog 2.1.0

Bug fixes

  • classify_review() classified the clips wrongly on Windows when review_dir had backslashes (e.g. E:\validation\clips): the name of the review folder entered the search for the verdict, so a folder named after a verdict marked every clip with it.

Warnings and diagnostics

  • fit_calibration() warns when the fitted GLMM is singular (a variance estimated at zero or a correlation at +-1); calibrate() passes the warning on.
  • compare_calibration_models() warns about, and counts in the new column n_failed, the folds whose fit failed; before, they were silently left out of the mean AUC.
  • calibration_effort() warns when n_train exceeds the smallest site x species cell minus five, and returns n_train_mean, n_test_mean and n_failed.
  • The documentation of select_clips() explains that target_total gives rare species higher inclusion probabilities (weight pooled estimates by 1 / inclusion_prob) and that the default recording_fraction = 0.01 draws one recording per site in small projects.

Documentation

  • New articles, run on a simulated example data set: vignette("sheepdog") (Get started), vignette("sampling-designs"), vignette("validation-effort"), vignette("calibration"), vignette("community-matrices") and vignette("retraining") (training folders for BirdNET-Analyzer from the reviewed clips).
  • The example data set (4 sites x 8 species x 6 months; selection tables, the list of recordings, reviewed clips and a calibrated nightly history) ships in system.file("extdata", "example", package = "sheepdog"); data-raw/make_example_data.R generates it.
  • plot_precision() draws one line per site when the table has several sites; before, the lines of different sites were joined in the same panel (also in the precision_by_bin.png of post_validation()).
  • vignette("community-matrices") uses a PCoA on square-root Bray-Curtis (ape::pcoa()) and a binomial GLLVM (‘gllvm’) for a model-based ordination and a test of the season effect; ‘ape’, ‘gllvm’ and ‘vegan’ are suggested packages, used only there.
  • The vignette crywolf-contract is now crywolf-integration (“Integration with crywolf”).
  • The repository was renamed to diogoprov/sheepdog; the package site is https://provetelab.org/sheepdog/.
  • The package can be installed from r-universe (install.packages("sheepdog", repos = c("https://diogoprov.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))), with binaries for Windows, macOS and Linux.

Tests

  • The comparisons with the v1.2.0 outputs tolerate floating-point differences between platforms (relative tolerance 1e-3 for the calibration outputs, 1e-8 for the others); R CMD check runs on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu in GitHub Actions.

sheepdog 2.0.0

The four scripts of birdnet-validation-sampler v1.2.0 become the R package sheepdog. With the same settings and seed, the package writes the same tables as v1.2.0, after the renaming below; the test suite checks this against outputs of the v1.2.0 scripts on simulated data. The scripts are preserved in the v1.2.0 tag.

From scripts to functions

v1.2.0 script sheepdog
extrair_clipes_validacao.R extract_validation_clips(); steps read_selection_tables(), select_clips(), cut_clips(), pack_clips()
pos_validacao.R post_validation(); steps classify_review(), precision_by_bin(), suggest_thresholds(), nightly_presence(), retraining_clips(), plot_precision()
calibracao.R calibrate(); steps read_validations(), calibration_models(), compare_calibration_models(), fit_calibration(), calibration_effort(), score_detections(), detection_history(), summarise_history(), plot_calibration()
gerar_matrizes_comunidade.R build_community_matrices(); step community_matrices()

select_clips() is a pure function: it returns the clip manifest without reading or writing audio.

Settings become arguments

Defaults are those of the config blocks, except project paths and project-specific lists, which are now required arguments (or NULL).

v1.2.0 config argument
dir_dados, padrao_tabela data_dir, table_pattern
dir_saida output_dir
modo_amostragem sampling_mode
unidade_ocasiao ("arquivo", "minuto") occasion_unit ("file", "minute")
limiar threshold
n_top n_top
fracao_gravacoes, n_gravacoes_por_local recording_fraction, n_recordings_per_site
tabela_gravacoes, padrao_audio, duracao_gravacao recordings, audio_pattern, recording_duration
conf_minima min_confidence
locais, especies sites, species
data_inicio, data_fim date_start, date_end
hora_inicio, hora_fim hour_start, hour_end
alternar_dias alternate_days
meta_total, max_por_especie target_total, max_per_species
balancear_por_hora balance_by_hour
remap_de, remap_para remap_from, remap_to
fazer_zip, simular make_zip, simulate
seed 2026 (fixed) seed = 2026
dir_validado, caminho_manifesto review_dir, manifest_path
padrao_positivo, padrao_negativo positive_pattern, negative_pattern
faixas, precisao_alvo, n_minimo bins, target_precision, min_n
arquivos_validacao, tabelas_predicao validation_files, prediction_tables
normalizar_locais site_map (default NULL)
p_min, min_deteccoes_noite, hora_madrugada p_min, min_detections_night, dawn_hour
k_folds, semente k_folds, seed
fazer_curva_esforco, esforco_n, esforco_repeticoes effort_curve, effort_n, effort_reps
arquivo_historico history_file
k_min, especies_nucleo, min_noites_mes k_min, core_species (required), min_nights_month

Output files, columns and values in English

  • Files: manifesto_clipes.csv → clip_manifest.csv; validacao_por_clipe.csv → validation_by_clip.csv; precisao_por_faixa → precision_by_bin; thresholds_sugeridos → suggested_thresholds; presenca_por_noite → nightly_presence; clipes_para_retreino → retraining_clips; comparacao_modelos → model_comparison; modelo_calibracao → calibration_model; curvas_calibradas → calibration_curves; curva_esforco → effort_curve; deteccoes_calibradas_<local> → calibrated_detections_<site>; historico_deteccao_noite → nightly_detection_history; resumo_deteccao_especie_local → detection_summary; matriz_frequencia_local_mes_k<k> → frequency_matrix_site_month_k<k>; matriz_contagens_local_mes_k<k> → count_matrix_site_month_k<k>; esforco_local_mes → effort_site_month. Folders clipes/ and pacotes/ → clips/ and packages/.
  • Columns and values of the manifest and the validation table: see vignette("crywolf-contract"). Other columns: especie → species, data → date, hora → hour, n_deteccoes → n_detections, n_confiaveis → n_reliable, deteccao(_k1..k3) → detection(_k1..k3), faixa → bin, n_validados → n_reviewed, n_positivos → n_positive, precisao → precision, pouco_suporte → low_support, n_suporte → n_support, precisao_no_corte → precision_at_threshold, n_clipes → n_clips, presenca → presence (confirmed, not_detected_in_reviewed, not_reviewed), conf_max_positivo → max_confidence_positive, modelo → model, auc_media/auc_dp → auc_mean/auc_sd, n_por_celula → n_per_cell, noites(_k1..k3) → nights(_k1..k3), mes → month, n_noites_gravadas → n_nights_recorded, incluido → included, n_noites_deteccao → n_nights_detected, frequencia → frequency.
  • Calibration models: m1_int_especie → m1_species_intercept, m2_slope_especie → m2_species_slope, m3_mais_local → m3_plus_site, m4_especie_x_local → m4_species_x_site; the model terms use species and site.
  • Whole-recording clips are named rec_... instead of grav_....
  • Messages, warnings and errors are in English.

Reading v1.2.0 files

post_validation(), classify_review(), calibrate(), read_validations(), community_matrices() and build_community_matrices() read manifests, validation tables and histories written by v1.2.0 and rename them on reading, so validated data stay usable.

Changes in behaviour

  • Random draws use withr::with_seed(): the draws are those of v1.2.0, and the global random number generator is left as it was.
  • suggest_thresholds() returns an empty table when no reviewed clip has a confidence score (whole recordings only); v1.2.0 wrote a row of NA.
  • The verdict patterns of the review are case-insensitive and only match the subfolders below review_dir, not the review folder itself.
  • A manifest without a confidence column is accepted.
  • score_detections() warns about prediction tables named after a site that is not in the calibration, and keeps the site name in the output.
  • The random-effects models of the calibration need ‘lme4’, and the package now stops when it is missing instead of letting those fits fail.
  • ‘av’, ‘lme4’ and ‘ggplot2’ are suggested packages, needed only to cut audio, to fit hierarchical models and to draw the figures.
